recoveryGates.title: Independent review recovery for Phases 11-20
acceptance: A fresh reviewer receives the manifest, product goal, current tree and reproducible commands without the implementer's success narrative.
Every Phase 11-20 exit claim is checked against current artifacts and meaningful mutation, failure or normal-route evidence where applicable.
Findings are repaired and rerun, with original false claims preserved as history rather than silently rewritten.
A durable batch report records findings, alternatives, verification, limitations and rollback.
recoveryGates.outcome: Six independent reviewers, no implementer narrative. 5 of 10 phases were NOT complete as claimed; 64 defects found, 62 repaired and mutation-proven, 3 registered as needing more than a repair. Python 1,375 -> 1,437; Swift 293 -> 335. REC-OPERATIONS remains open: the mixed-backlog grouping still needs Nick's approval before anything is staged, and no commit or push was made.

recoveryGates.title: Tangible v2 backend foundation
recoveryGates.when: before enabling real v2 connector, write, automation or remote-control paths; stage the read-only service before any write/control activation
acceptance: Nick chooses the host, database, authentication and operations approach with cost and local/cloud boundaries visible.
A running API and database use owner-scoped durable repositories rather than in-memory stand-ins.
Production-quality authenticated encryption and signature verification adapters are installed through reviewed dependencies or platform services.
Restart, migration, offline/retry, monitoring and rollback behavior are proven through the normal route.
A provider operations dashboard or equivalent is distinguished from Orion's own product UI.

recoveryGates.title: Authority, approval consumption and replay safety
recoveryGates.when: before live Calendar/Gmail writes, automatic communications or remote control
acceptance: A sufficiently specific direct request authorizes the requested action and ordinary in-scope use of already-enabled capabilities without duplicate approval.
Each consequential approval is bound to canonical content, actor, target, expiry and nonce and is consumed once.
Retries are idempotent and cannot repeat a completed side effect.
Approval, execution, denial, revocation and recovery survive restart in an inspectable audit trail.
Automatic modes are explicit, scoped, visible, expiring, revocable and immediately stoppable; preferences never grant authority.

recoveryGates.title: First real read-only integration slice
recoveryGates.when: in the first connected-product batch, before enabling broader v2 connector actions
acceptance: A chosen least-privilege read-only connector runs through the deployed v2 path with real provider responses, revocation, audit and failure evidence.
Google transport is not inferred from request builders or parsers.

A first Google read does not depend on HealthKit. Before enabling the separate HealthKit feature, prove local acquisition and required entitlement/privacy behavior; raw measurements remain inside the health boundary.
No write, send, monitoring or recurring automation is enabled by this checkpoint.

recoveryGates.title: Visible usable client slice
recoveryGates.when: in the first connected-product batch, before expanding to broad live automation; it is not deferred to Phase 84
acceptance: A real SwiftUI iPhone target renders and runs in the simulator or on device; MobileCore compilation alone is insufficient.
The current block, next step, plan changes/reasons, focus state and important items are understandable in the home/planner experience.
A desktop/mobile settings and control path exposes synchronized state, revocation and the local emergency stop without uploading all private content.
A small end-to-end normal-route action crosses visible UI, backend boundary, durable state and truthful result with restart/offline/retry evidence.

recoveryGates.title: Reviewed batch checkpoint and recovery operations
recoveryGates.when: at each roughly ten-phase batch and before release claims
acceptance: Independent review and repairs are recorded in a durable readable batch report.
Source and history secret scans pass before a commit checkpoint.
Unrelated user-owned changes are separated and no historical commit or timestamp is fabricated.
Commit and push are recorded separately; a local commit is never called a remote backup.
Rollback, restore and monitoring evidence are reproducible.

continuationOrder.work: Review Phases 11-20, repair findings, and write the mixed-backlog grouping and checkpoint plan. Establish a reviewed local baseline with approved scope before resuming another large batch.

Plan the first connected-product batch: obtain Nick's provider/budget and first-feature decisions; implement staged API/auth/database/persistence plus the minimal visible home/planner. UI prototypes can precede live connections. Dependencies and acceptance must be written before implementation.

Connect one approved read-only source to the visible client, prove ownership/isolation, revocation, restart/offline/retry behavior and truthful results. Independently review and checkpoint the batch before broader activation.

Resume the remaining numbered phases under the amended scope. Close approval-consumption and durable-authority gaps before real writes, autonomous messages or remote control. Phase 33 still precedes 34 within the unchanged numbered sequence.

capabilityHomes.title: School, full-day planning and focus
capabilityHomes.amendment: Add source-aware classes and assignments, progress uncertainty, optional full-day scheduling with intentional free time, transitions, completion-aware replanning and a comprehensible current/next home surface.

capabilityHomes.title: Proactivity, availability and optional presence
capabilityHomes.amendment: Add explicit interruption modes, quiet hours, alert budgets and minimally invasive local presence options. Camera/location remain unselected future evaluations with consent and retention unresolved.

capabilityHomes.title: Media, reversible computer work and home control
capabilityHomes.amendment: Add quick preference-aware media action, non-destructive desktop organization with undo/collision protection, and smart-home capability under certified-device and reviewed-authority boundaries. Remote access never bypasses Mac security.

capabilityHomes.title: Memory, local models, response quality and cost
capabilityHomes.amendment: Add hardware benchmarks, compact relevant retrieval, inspectable preferences, latency/cost budgets and deterministic no-LLM paths. Candidate local model sizes are not provider selections or quality claims.

capabilityHomes.title: Communications and personal-assistant mode
capabilityHomes.amendment: Add reviewed-to-delegated texting progression and a disclosed call-assistant mode that always identifies as Orion, Nick's assistant. Provider feasibility, privacy law, cost, audiences and exceptions remain open.

capabilityHomes.title: Tangible backend and visible product
capabilityHomes.amendment: Add early running-backend and usable-client checkpoints. Preserve Phase 16/19 historical contract closures while requiring actual rendered screens and normal-route proof before product claims.

capabilityHomes.title: Explicit future ideas
capabilityHomes.amendment: Retain battery charge limiting, visa-email alerts, finance subscriptions, consent-aware recording/notes, conversational styles, remote dispatch and context-sensitive help as unimplemented aspirations requiring their own feasibility, privacy, provider and authority decisions.

programCorrection.title: Program correction — ordering superseded

programCorrection.finding: The manifest contains zero occurrences of 'OpenClaw' in 2,644 lines and its Phase 0 inventoried a Python runtime that the running assistant's own memory had already declared not-the-implementation-path on 2026-07-28. The requirements are sound; the ORDERING is derived from an inventory of a system that was not running.
programCorrection.supersedes: the manifest's phase ordering only. Not its requirements, not the fingerprint, not any closed phase.
programCorrection.keyCorrection: ORION Core already exists, in TypeScript, on the live route: permissions.ts + validator.ts + provenance.ts + outcome.ts + the append-only ledger. orion/security/profiles.py already concedes this in its own docstring. Phase 1's exit gate should be closed by re-pointing the record onto the live gate and demoting the Python engine to a conformance oracle -- not by a cross-language rewrite.
